compound.name: chamazulene
compound.one_liner: The blue of chamomile oil, formed from colourless matricin during steam distillation.

identity.note: formed_during: steam distillation (from matricin), confirmed by EMA assessment report.

biosynthesis.pathway: MVA/terpenoid (sesquiterpene; from farnesyl diphosphate); formed from matricin
biosynthesis.note: Not biosynthesised as such: proazulenes are at least partly converted to chamazulene during steam distillation [10].

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Matricaria recutita L., flos and Matricaria recutita L., aetheroleum. EMA/HMPC/55837/2011 (7 Jul 2015). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-matricaria-recutita-l-flos-and-matricaria-recutita-l-aetheroleum-first-version_en.pdf-0
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: EMA: 'proazulenes like matricin and matricarin ... are at least partially converted during steam distillation into azulenes like chamazulene'. Duke: CHAMAZULENE Flower 530-13200 ppm (a distillation product, so best read as oil-derived). | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil | Formed during steam distillation; no claim is made about presence or absence in an infusion (TODO(author)).

pharmacology.mechanism: Inhibited leukotriene B4 synthesis by 50 % at 15 µM in rat neutrophils [10].

evidence.claim: Chamazulene inhibits leukotriene B4 formation in neutrophils.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Presence or absence in an infusion is not claimed; EMA states matricin itself is extracted into teas [10].

compound.teaching_note: A processing artefact with a colour: the flower is not blue, the oil is [10].
gaps: Presence/absence in tea unknown (TODO(author)); chamazulene carboxylic acid route not sourced.
